why: All three checks pass and no refutation was found. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at skills.md:637 under the heading '### Override skill visibility from settings'. The whole line is three sentences and none of them reverses the conclusion: 'The `skillOverrides` setting controls skill visibility from your [settings](/docs/en/settings) instead of the skill's own frontmatter. Use it for skills whose SKILL.md you don't want to edit, such as ones checked into a shared project repo. The `/skills` menu writes it for you: highlight a skill and press `Space` to cycle states, then `Enter` to save to `.claude/settings.local.json`.' The four-state table (on / name-only / user-invocable-only / off), 'A skill that is absent from `skillOverrides` is treated as "on"' (:652) and the v2.1.199 SDK/Remote-Control clause (:650) are all present as claimed. (2) The cited repo evidence is accurate: `grep -ran skillOverrides` (with -a, so NUL-bearing files are not skipped) hits docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193 and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:264,:559 plus this sweep's own output files. Zero hits under packages/ or apps/. A case-insensitive sweep for every plausible Nessy renaming of the key (skilloverride, skill_override, skillVisibility, name-only/nameOnly, user-invocable-only/userInvocableOnly) finds no settings key of any spelling; packages/shared/src/config/{storage.ts,validators.ts,config-defaults.json} and pi-harness/managed-policy.ts carry no skill-visibility key at all. (3) One layer up and down, the CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier and it holds for the subsystem named. Candidate refutations checked and each ruled out: (a) Plugin capabilities DO have a persisted settings-side toggle (`setCapabilityEnabled` -> capabilities.json via packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts, tri-state per scope global<workspace<project with a managed tier on top) - but that store's own docblock scopes it to plugin capabilities, its PolicyTarget is {pluginKey, pluginInstanceId}, and Claude's page explicitly exempts plugin skills ('Plugin skills are not affected by `skillOverrides`. Manage those through `/plugin` instead.'), so this is the sibling subsystem, not the mechanism, and it cannot reach a native SKILL.md. (b) Native capabilities in resolver.ts:1595 derive `enabled` from `record.sourceEnabled`, which native-sources.ts sets only from a Source's `sources/<slug>/config.json` `enabled` field - skills have no such config file. (c) The only other native disable path is `sessionSelection.transientlyDisabledKeys` (resolver.ts:739,:1574,:1618,:1774), which is transient by design AND has no producer anywhere outside resolver.ts - so even the session-scoped half is unwired. (d) `Skill(name)` permission rules are not an escape either: `Skill` appears in BUILT_IN_TOOLS (pre-tool-use.ts:134) but there is no `Skill` entry in PI_TOOL_BINDINGS, from which PERMISSION_RULE_TOOL_NAMES is derived, and skills are invoked via `[skill:name]` markers through extractModelSkillInvocations, not through a permission-gated `Skill` tool. (e) Project detect-consent (capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts) and project trust are per-project and all-or-nothing (and resolver.ts:1623 applies trustState only to `kind === 'hook'`), not a per-skill override. (f) The model-facing listing, prompt-builder.ts buildSkillListingPart, filters solely on `disableModelInvocation` - a frontmatter field - confirming the listing side reads no settings override. Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns skill visibility (they are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions). Not a deliberate fork difference either: skill visibility is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ renaming. On the contrary, the parity audit itself names this gap - 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1651 lists 'settings-level "restrict skill access" and "override skill visibility"' among what P7/P9 closed their frontmatter rows without, routed to R30a; R30's closure notes cover argument substitution, `effort`, `paths` and the /doctor surface, and never mention shipping skillOverrides. So the row is marked done on a scope that never included this half.
correctedState: Confirmed, with two refinements to the wording. (1) The absence is exact for NATIVE skills: no reader of `skillOverrides` or of any renamed equivalent exists in packages/ or apps/; the string occurs only in planning documents (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-session-scheduling.md:193, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-r-queue-doc-verification.md:264,:559) and in this sweep's own generated artifacts. None of the four states (on / name-only / user-invocable-only / off) exists, absent-means-on is vacuous, and nothing hides a skill from any command list from settings. (2) The claim should name the subsystem, because a sibling one is implemented: PLUGIN capabilities (including plugin-bundled skills) DO have a persisted, scoped settings-side enable/disable via packages/shared/src/plugins/management-service-v2.ts `setCapabilityEnabled` and packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts (global < workspace < project, plus a terminal managed tier), which is exactly the surface Claude's page routes plugin skills to. The gap is therefore: a non-plugin skill - workspace `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`, global `~/.agents/skills/`, or one checked into a shared repo at `.agents/skills/` - has no settings-side visibility control of any kind. Its only levers are frontmatter (`disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, both honoured: prompt-builder.ts buildSkillListingPart filters on `disableModelInvocation`), deleting the file, or untrusting the whole project via detect-consent, which is all-or-nothing per project rather than per skill. The nearest native hook, `sessionSelection.transientlyDisabledKeys` (resolver.ts:739,:1574,:1618,:1774), is transient by design and additionally has no producer, so it is not even a partial substitute. Also worth recording against the tracker: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1651 already identifies 'override skill visibility' as an unclosed part of R30a, so the parity row is marked done over a scope that excluded it.
